title: Left-Facing Fist Emoji 🤛 Meaning: The Other Half of a Bump
description: The left-facing fist emoji 🤛 is the half of a fist bump that comes in to meet 🤜. See what it means alone, how to order the pair, and when it turns into a punch.
summary: 🤛 shows a closed fist with its knuckles aimed to the left. It usually means a fist bump: respect, solidarity, “nice one” or “we’re good.” Placed after 🤜, the two fists meet in the middle to complete the bump. On its own it can also answer a fist bump someone else started.
meaning: Direction is the whole point of this emoji. 🤛 points left, so it acts as the receiving fist when it follows a right-facing 🤜. Typed in that order, 🤜🤛, the knuckles collide in the middle of the line and the bump is complete. Reversed, 🤛🤜, the fists point away from each other, which looks like a missed connection, so most people stick to the first order.

Alone, 🤛 works much like 👊: a casual sign of respect between friends, teammates or gamers. It says “good game,” “proud of you” or “we’re cool” without the sentimentality of a heart. Some people send it as a reply to a friend’s 🤜, letting two separate messages finish the gesture across the conversation, a small and satisfying bit of digital body language.

A fist can also mean a punch, and 🤛 is occasionally used that way in jokes, fight banter or combat-sports chat, often next to 💥. That reading is clearly secondary. Because the emoji is drawn in profile rather than head-on, it looks more like a bump in motion than a blow coming at the viewer, which keeps the overall tone friendly.

It was added in 2016 together with its mirror image, and the pair filled a real gap. Before them, people had only the knuckles-forward 👊 and the upright ✊, and neither showed two people connecting. Like most hand emojis, 🤛 supports skin tones, so two friends can bump fists in their own shades within a single line of text.

contexts.label: Between friends
contexts.body: A quick 🤛 after a favor or a good joke acknowledges it without any fuss. It is especially common among people who prefer a fist bump to hearts, though it is used across ages and genders. Replying 🤛 to a friend’s 🤜 completes the gesture and has become a small, satisfying ritual in many chats.

contexts.label: In gaming and sports
contexts.body: Teammates send 🤜🤛 before a match and after a win, and coaches drop it into team group chats to say “good work today.” In fight-sport discussions a single fist can stand for a jab, especially alongside 🥊 or 💥. Even in those spaces, the supportive fist bump remains the more common meaning by a wide margin.

contexts.label: In captions
contexts.body: Posts about friendship, partnerships or teamwork use 🤜🤛 as shorthand for a solid bond: “ten years of being business partners 🤜🤛.” It suggests loyalty and equal footing without the romance a heart might imply. That makes it a good fit for friend groups, sports clubs and coworkers celebrating a shared win together.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: In casual workplace chat, a fist bump is a friendly way to thank a colleague or mark a finished project. It is less formal than a thumbs-up and a notch more enthusiastic. With senior people or clients you do not know well, 👍 or a short written thank-you is the safer option.

confusedWith.difference: 🤜 is the mirror image, pointing right. It usually comes first in a bump, with 🤛 answering it. The meanings are the same; the only difference is direction, which matters once you place them side by side.
👊 shows a fist coming straight at the viewer. It can be a bump or a punch and needs no partner. 🤛 is drawn sideways, so it reads more clearly as one half of a two-person gesture.
✊ is a fist held upright, a symbol of solidarity, protest and power. 🤛 is a horizontal fist for bumping. Using ✊ for a casual “nice one” can unintentionally sound political.

avoid: Do not type 🤛 before 🤜 if you mean a fist bump, because the fists will point away from each other.
Avoid it in condolence messages, where a fist bump can feel too casual.
Skip the punch meaning with people who might take a fist as a real threat.
design: A closed hand seen from the side, knuckles pointing left, with the thumb curled across the front of the fingers. It uses the same default yellow as other hand emojis and supports all five skin tones. Styles range from flat cartoon to shaded and detailed, but the leftward direction is consistent, and on most platforms it mirrors 🤜 so the pair fits together cleanly.

faqs.q: What does 🤛 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Usually respect, thanks or “we’re good.” Many guys prefer a fist bump to more emotional emojis, so it is a sign of friendly approval. It has no romantic meaning by itself, though it can be a warm gesture between close friends.

faqs.q: Which order do the fist bump emojis go in?
faqs.a: Right-facing first, then left-facing: 🤜🤛. That way the knuckles point toward each other and meet in the middle. If the order is reversed, the fists point outward and the bump visually misses.

faqs.q: Is 🤛 a punch or a fist bump?
faqs.a: Almost always a fist bump. The punch reading shows up mainly in jokes and combat-sports chat, typically made clear by 💥 or 🥊. In everyday conversation, assume friendliness unless the words around it are hostile.

faqs.q: When was the left-facing fist emoji added?
faqs.a: It was added in 2016, as part of Emoji 3.0, together with its mirror image, the right-facing fist. The pair was designed so that two fists could meet in a single line of text.
